Тривожно 🫂 First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine (@azov_media) The advance of two armies and a tank division of the Russian armed forces was repelled: forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine destroyed dozens of units of equipment and a large number of occupier personnel. On July 22, the occupiers, using forces of the 8th and 41st Armies along with the 90th Tank Division, attempted an assault in the sector held by the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, involving dozens of units of armored and light vehicles. The 41st Guards Combined Arms Army and the 90th Guards Vitebsk-Novgorod Tank Division of the Russian armed forces advanced from the area of the settlement of Novoekonomichne, while forces of the 8th Guards Combined Arms Army simultaneously advanced from the area of the village of Vozdvyzhenka. For four hours, they attempted to enter settlements in the area of the village of Shakhove. The enemy attempted to deny the sky to Ukrainian forces using "Gerbera" and "Lancet" strike drones. A modern Russian "Tornado-S" MLRS, which was being used to support the assault, was also destroyed. Forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, together with attached units, blocked the path of the advancing mechanized columns. Mine-explosive obstacles were laid on the approaches to the positions of the Ukrainian Defense Forces, and bridges were damaged by tactical aviation. During the assault, the Russians attempted to restore the crossings using pontoons, but these were destroyed by tactical aviation of the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU). As a result of the professional actions of all units involved under the command of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, using barrel artillery, multiple launch rocket systems, and attack drones, the following were destroyed: 7 tanks, 6 armored combat vehicles, 1 BM-21 "Grad" MLRS, 1 "Tornado-S" MLRS, 3 units of special equipment, and 47 units of light vehicles. 123 occupiers were eliminated, and 29 were wounded. The mechanized assault was repelled. We thank the units of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, the SBU's "A" Special Operations Center, the Unmanned Systems Forces, the Air Force of the AFU, units of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, in particular the Main Department of Unmanned Aerial Systems "Fenix," units of the National Guard of Ukraine, and units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine for their professional and courageous actions. The Thirty-Third Meeting of the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) was held in Manila, Philippines, on 23 July 2026. The Meeting was chaired by H.E. Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro, Secretary of Foreign Affairs of the Philippines, under the ASEAN 2026 Chairship theme of “Navigating Our Future, Together”. The Meeting was attended by the Foreign Ministers and Representatives of all ARF Participants, as well as the Secretary-General of ASEAN. The Meeting reaffirmed the ARF’s role as the leading ASEAN-led forum for fostering constructive dialogue and cooperation on political and security issues in the Asia-Pacific region, with ASEAN as its primary driving force. Amidst an increasingly interconnected and complex regional security environment, the Meeting underscored the importance of confidence-building and preventive diplomacy, as well as strengthening dialogue and fostering practical cooperation among ARF Participants. In this regard, the Meeting encouraged continued efforts to enhance the effectiveness and responsiveness of the ARF within the evolving regional architecture. Learn more: bit.ly/CS_33rdARF

The 27th ASEAN Plus Three Foreign Ministers’ Meeting was chaired by H.E. Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro, Secretary of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Philippines. The Meeting noted the progress in the ASEAN Plus Three (APT) cooperation over the past year and discussed its future direction. The Meeting reaffirmed the commitment to further strengthening and deepening the APT process, which remains a main vehicle for advancing regional community-building and in promoting peace, stability, security, and prosperity in the East Asian region with ASEAN as the driving force. The Meeting also recognised the importance of APT cooperation in supporting the realisation of ASEAN 2045: Our Shared Future and its strategic plans, the Initiative for ASEAN Integration (IAI) Work Plan IV (2021–2025), including their contributions to the development and implementation of the IAI Work Plan V (2026–2030), as well as deeper regional integration in East Asia. Learn more: bit.ly/CS_27thAPTFM

Scotland has just done something quietly brilliant for its birds 🐦 New buildings across the country will now have to include "swift bricks", hollow bricks built straight into the walls that give birds a safe place to nest. It sounds like a small thing but it isn't. Swift numbers in the UK have fallen by around 60% since the mid-1990s, and one of the biggest reasons is heartbreakingly simple: modern buildings have nowhere for them to go. Swifts have always nested in the nooks and gaps of our houses, and as those disappeared, so did they. The birds themselves make it worse by being loyal to a fault. Swifts return to the exact same nest site year after year, having flown thousands of miles from Africa to get there. When they arrive to find it sealed up, some will keep flying at the spot again and again, sometimes injuring themselves in the process. The bricks cost about £30 each. They need no maintenance, they don't affect insulation, and once they're in the wall, you'd never know they were there. Sparrows, starlings and house martins use them too, all species in trouble for the same reason. One RSPB conservationist put it starkly. In his part of Glasgow, not a single swift bred in 2025, the first time in his 30 years there. He called it "nothing short of heartbreaking." Scotland is the first country in the UK to write this into law. Campaigners are now hoping the rest follows.

MIT filmed a calculus course in black and white decades ago and it still teaches better than most of what shipped this year. Almost nobody watches it. This is Calculus Revisited, Unit 1, Lecture 1, taught by Herb Gross. Analytic geometry from the ground up, chalk on a board, 1 camera locked in place. Gross built the course for adults returning to math after years away. No prerequisites assumed. Every idea earned in front of you instead of quoted from a textbook. The opening move is simple division written on the board. From there he shows why coordinates work at all, the thing most courses skip and every student silently fakes. Watch how slowly he goes. Each step spoken out loud, nothing left implicit, the pace of someone who expects you to actually follow. A backend engineer I know rewatched Unit 1 twice before touching linear algebra and said it fixed a gap he'd carried for 12 years. MIT put the whole course online free under Creative Commons. BOOM! OPEN SOURCE MRI! You can now 3D-print the core of an MRI scanner. A machine that hospitals pay $1.1 million to $3.4 million for has been broken open. The OSI² ONE and its educational siblings deliver real images of heads and limbs for a fraction of the cost, using a permanent-magnet Halbach array, 3D-printed structures, and fully open designs. This is not a toy or a simulation. Working systems already produce in-vivo images in Leiden, Utrecht, Berlin, and Uganda. The magnet alone—396 carefully oriented neodymium cubes in a cylindrical Halbach array—costs about $1,370. A complete scanner lands between $28,500 and $68,000 depending on the console and coils you choose. No superconducting magnets. No liquid helium. No specialized power infrastructure. It runs from a standard wall outlet and weighs roughly 150 kg. The physics is elegant. A Halbach array arranges permanent magnets so their fields reinforce inside the bore and nearly cancel outside. The result is a usable 50 mT field strong enough for diagnostic-quality imaging of extremities and the head when paired with clever gradient coils, RF coils, and modern reconstruction. Spatial resolution reaches about 1.5 × 1.5 × 5 mm³. The designs are modular: build the magnet first, verify and shim the field with a 3D-printer-turned-field-scanner, then add gradients and RF hardware. The plans are public Everything needed to replicate or improve the system lives in open repositories: • Primary project hub and documentation: opensourceimaging.org/projec… • Full OSI² repositories (hardware, software, magnets): gitlab.com/osii/ • Educational build focused on the Halbach frame, shimming, gradients, and student workshops (Utrecht / Lili’s Proto Lab): github.com/LilisProtoLab/osi… • Magnet-specific details: opensourceimaging.org/projec… Hardware is released under CERN-OHL-W. Most software is GPL-3.0. Where AI multiplies the impact Low-field MRI has historically been limited by lower signal-to-noise and greater field inhomogeneity. That is exactly the regime where modern AI thrives. Image reconstruction becomes dramatically better when deep networks trained on high-field data or physics-informed models denoise, correct for inhomogeneity, and push resolution beyond the raw acquisition limits. Real-time sequence adaptation can adjust gradients and RF pulses on the fly as the AI monitors signal quality. Magnet design itself can be optimized by evolutionary algorithms or differentiable physics engines that search for better Halbach geometries or shim placements than human intuition alone can find. Further out, local AI agents turn these scanners into autonomous diagnostic nodes. A small clinic or even a well-equipped garage workshop could run overnight scans, flag anomalies, and queue results for a remote radiologist—or eventually for a specialized medical model. Synthetic data generation from the open designs lets researchers train robust models without proprietary hospital datasets. Robotics integration (patient positioning, coil placement, maintenance) becomes straightforward once the hardware is open and standardized. In the longer arc of the Abundance Interregnum, this is the shape of things: sophisticated medical instruments that no longer require billion-dollar supply chains or national infrastructure. A distributed network of open, AI-augmented low-field scanners could bring advanced imaging to places that have never had it, while simultaneously giving makers, universities, and small labs the ability to experiment, improve, and specialize the technology. The plans are already on the table. The magnets are commercial off-the-shelf. The 3D printers exist in thousands of workshops. The AI tools for reconstruction and design optimization improve every month. What was once the exclusive domain of major hospitals is becoming a community engineering project. This is how abundance arrives—one open, reproducible, AI-extendable system at a time.

No meu discurso de posse em janeiro de 2023 resgatei, porque foi necessário, um compromisso que já havia assumido e honrado nos primeiros dois mandatos: garantir os preceitos constitucionais do direito a uma vida digna, sem fome. Os dados revelados pelo Mapa da Fome da ONU nesta semana reforçam que estamos cumprindo esta missão. Entre 2023 e 2025, o Brasil reduziu em mais de 90% o número de pessoas em insegurança alimentar grave, para 0,6%. O índice chegou a 8,5% nos tempos em que o país retornou ao Mapa da Fome. O resultado é retrato de uma articulação de 80 ações e programas de vários ministérios, com foco no acesso à renda, proteção social e apoio à produção e ao consumo de alimentos adequados, tudo em torno do Plano Brasil sem Fome. Fazem parte dessa equação tanto iniciativas mais conhecidas, como Bolsa Família e Gás do Povo, quanto o Programa de Aquisição de Alimentos, o reajuste e a qualificação da merenda escolar, a volta do financiamento à agricultura familiar, as cozinhas solidárias, o fomento rural, o programa Cisternas, o BPC e o Luz do Povo, para citar alguns. Não à toa, os resultados do Mapa da Fome se conectam com indicadores macroeconômicos que permitem essa melhora da condição de vida de milhões de brasileiros. O PIB acumulou altas nos três últimos anos, a taxa de desemprego registra os menores dados da série histórica, o rendimento médio mensal real domiciliar alcançou o maior valor já registrado pelo IBGE e o salário mínimo voltou a ter ganho real. Como disse naquele discurso de posse, os direitos e interesses da população, o fortalecimento da democracia e a retomada da soberania nacional são pilares de nosso governo.

The advance of two armies and a tank division of the Russian armed forces was repelled: forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine destroyed dozens of units of equipment and a large number of occupier personnel. On July 22, the occupiers, using forces of the 8th and 41st Armies along with the 90th Tank Division, attempted an assault in the sector held by the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, involving dozens of units of armored and light vehicles. The 41st Guards Combined Arms Army and the 90th Guards Vitebsk-Novgorod Tank Division of the Russian armed forces advanced from the area of the settlement of Novoekonomichne, while forces of the 8th Guards Combined Arms Army simultaneously advanced from the area of the village of Vozdvyzhenka. For four hours, they attempted to enter settlements in the area of the village of Shakhove. The enemy attempted to deny the sky to Ukrainian forces using "Gerbera" and "Lancet" strike drones. A modern Russian "Tornado-S" MLRS, which was being used to support the assault, was also destroyed. Forces of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, together with attached units, blocked the path of the advancing mechanized columns. Mine-explosive obstacles were laid on the approaches to the positions of the Ukrainian Defense Forces, and bridges were damaged by tactical aviation. During the assault, the Russians attempted to restore the crossings using pontoons, but these were destroyed by tactical aviation of the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU). As a result of the professional actions of all units involved under the command of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, using barrel artillery, multiple launch rocket systems, and attack drones, the following were destroyed: 7 tanks, 6 armored combat vehicles, 1 BM-21 "Grad" MLRS, 1 "Tornado-S" MLRS, 3 units of special equipment, and 47 units of light vehicles. 123 occupiers were eliminated, and 29 were wounded. The mechanized assault was repelled. We thank the units of the First Corps Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, the SBU's "A" Special Operations Center, the Unmanned Systems Forces, the Air Force of the AFU, units of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, in particular the Main Department of Unmanned Aerial Systems "Fenix," units of the National Guard of Ukraine, and units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine for their professional and courageous actions. Russian feedback about using UGVs🔽 1. Before using the UGV, it is necessary to review the route of movement with the UAV for the purpose of passability. UGV can be stuck relatively easily. It is impossible to simply direct the UGV in a certain direction, as is done with tanks or IGVs. This will most likely lead to the loss of the drone. 2. Basically, UGVs are used for restraining actions (distracting attention); in order to maneuver, the group could strike from a second direction. The enemy always hits the UGV, even when they do not pose a real threat to the enemy's strongholds. Machine-gun UGVs cannot defeat soldiers in a trench. UGVs with AGS-17 have limited ammunition and cannot take part in the battle for a long time. The absence of significant targets leads to the fact that the UAV operators still try to defeat the UGV. This allows you to use them to call FPV drone strikes on yourself. 3. If possible, the UGV will drive as close as possible to the point of launch on a cargo vehicle. 4. UGVs break down a lot. Spare batteries and control antennas (retranslators) are needed in large quantities. 5. A UGV is operated by the calculation of 2–3 people. 6. Unlike analog FPV drones, which react almost instantly to control commands, UGVs can react with a delay. Digital channels are used in UGV controls, which often introduce such a delay. 7. UAVs are used to accompany the movement of the UGV. Visibility from the ground is usually insufficient for controlling a UGV. 8. The UGV controlled by radio channels, like the UAVs, requires installation of control antennas and the use of repeaters. 9. It happens that a scheme is being implemented in which the UGV is moving forward on fiber optic and comes back with the help of a management UAV. The duplicating control system, which allows controlling the UGV from the UAV, is also necessary due to the fact that the quality of the cable unwound for the UGV can be low. This, in particular, can lead to the fact that after 200 meters of movement, the image will disappear.

Heatwaves don't just bring high temperatures; they can also increase drowning risk. Hot weather draws more people to the water, and you may be tempted to: 🔹 Stay in the water for longer or more frequent periods 🔹 Swim unsupervised in open water or take other risks around water 🔹 Enter cold water suddenly, especially when the air feels hot How to stay safe: ✅ Choose supervised places to swim ✅ Don’t drink alcohol near water ✅ Always where a life jacket while boating ✅ Enter unfamiliar or cold water gradually ✅ If you fall in or are shocked by cold, float on your back and control your breathing before trying to swim ✅ Always keep children within close, constant supervision around water #DrowningPrevention #WorldDrowningPreventionDay 📷 Getty Images

LOOK: The University of the Philippines' Institute for Maritime Affairs and Law of the Sea (IMLOS) has released an updated edition of its West Philippine Sea primer, offering a "concise yet comprehensive" guide to the territorial and maritime disputes from the Philippine perspective. Titled "The West Philippine Sea: The Territorial and Maritime Jurisdiction Disputes from a Filipino Perspective (The WPS Primer 2026)," the 95-page publication builds on the original primer released in 2013 by IMLOS and the UP Asian Center. It incorporates major developments over the past decade, including the landmark 2016 South China Sea Arbitration ruling, which affirmed the Philippines' sovereign rights and jurisdiction over its exclusive economic zone in the West Philippine Sea. The primer is available for free download through the IMLOS website. (📷: UP IMLOS/Facebook)

🔥 Au cœur des feux de forêt, un seul objectif : protéger la population. Engagés en Gironde aux côtés du SDIS 33, les sapeurs-pompiers de Paris poursuivent leur mission dans des conditions particulièrement éprouvantes. Face à un incendie encore difficilement maîtrisable, les équipes sont pleinement mobilisées pour protéger les habitations, contenir la progression des flammes et participer aux évacuations lorsque la situation l'exige. Sur le terrain, les sapeurs-pompiers de Paris, du SDIS 77 et de la Gironde travaillent main dans la main. Au-delà des uniformes et des écussons, c'est une même mission qui les rassemble : préserver des vies, protéger les biens et soutenir les populations confrontées à cette épreuve. Dans ce type d'intervention, chaque geste compte. La coordination, la confiance et la solidarité entre les équipes sont des forces essentielles pour faire face à un feu imprévisible, où les conditions peuvent évoluer en quelques instants. Les journées sont longues, les températures élevées et l'engagement physique est intense. Mais ensemble, les femmes et les hommes engagés sur le terrain avancent avec la même détermination, animés par un seul objectif : remplir leur mission jusqu'au bout. 👏 Courage à l'ensemble des sapeurs-pompiers mobilisés en Gironde. Drowning claims around 300,000 lives every year. That is 30 people every hour. Nearly 1 in 4 are children under 5. As heatwaves become more frequent, more people seek relief in rivers, lakes and the sea, increasing their exposure to drowning risks. Yet drowning is largely preventable. This year’s World Drowning Prevention Day theme, “Unite to turn the tide”, calls for governments, communities and individuals to work together to reduce the toll. Between 2000 and 2021, the global drowning death rate fell by 38%, showing what sustained efforts can achieve. The first-ever Global Strategy for Drowning Prevention aims to build on this progress, targeting 35% fewer deaths by 2035. Governments can accelerate progress by expanding supervised childcare and swimming education, making water sources and pools safer, strengthening flood warnings and safety standards for water transport. Each of us also has a part to play: watch children closely around water, use lifejackets, learn to swim and develop water-safety skills, and never underestimate the risks. These actions can spare thousands of families a devastating loss.

Let's unpack the options for what the US government could do to potentially restrict Chinese AI models: 1. FUD: @deanwball noted the other day that the US government could take a "FUD" approach of just creating lots of doubt and uncertainty about use of Chinese AI, rather than strict legal requirements. (Dean made this point as an analytic matter, he was not advocating for it). The government could issue public security advisories, get sectoral regulators like energy and financial regulators to start raising risks, etc. This might not legally prohibit use, but would likely discourage it. 2. Procurement bans: The U.S. government could use procurement authorities to prohibit the use of Chinese AI models in government contracts, similar to what DoD did to Anthropic earlier this year. This would not prohibit private companies from using Chinese AI models unrelated to government contracts, but it would discourage use and reinforce a FUD approach. 3. Entity List: The Commerce Department could put specific Chinese AI companies (Moonshot, etc.) on the Entity List, which would prohibit exports of US technology to them. Setting aside evasion, this would cut off their access to any remaining US-origin chips not already covered by more general export controls and to US software. It would also potentially complicate U.S. companies’ use of closed or hosted models, as a US company could not send its own software or other "items" to the Chinese company for processing. It would not, however, strictly legally prohibit a U.S. company from downloading an open source model that a Chinese AI company posted online, as the download would not be an export *to* China, but rather an import from it. 4. "ICTS" rule: Commerce's existing "ICTS rule" allows Commerce to restrict the import or US use of a variety of software and other technology that poses a national security risk. Commerce has used the ICTS rule to, inter alia, prevent Americans from using Kaspersky Lab software (from Russia) and it is the basis for the recently-in-the-news restrictions on Polestar autos. Commerce could in theory deploy the rule to prohibit US firms from using Chinese AI models in the US. The one potential caveat to this is that the ICTS Rule exists pursuant to IEEPA, and IEEPA cannot regulate the import (or export) of "information" or "informational materials." I think courts would almost certainly uphold the ICTS rule as applied to the import or use of Chinese-hosted AI models as a prohibition on a “service,” and not on “information.” There would, however, be an interesting question about whether the courts would uphold a ban on a simple US download of an open-source Chinese model, where there was no payment. 5. Sanctions on Chinese AI labs: The President could use IEEPA to impose sanctions on Chinese AI labs, likely after declaring a new national emergency related to adversarial country AI risks. This would block their property in the US and prohibit all US commercial transactions with them. However, IEEPA sanctions would have the same carve out for "information" or "informational materials" as applies to the ICTS rule, and there is some chance the courts would find that IEEPA sanctions cannot prevent a US company from downloading, for free, an open source Chinese model. (Courts, for example, blocked Trump's 2020 use of IEEPA to try to restrict TikTok in the United States). 6. New IEEPA-derived restrictions on US companies using/deploying Chinese AI models: IEEPA is a flexible statute and the Trump Administration could use IEEPA to create new restrictions on the use or deployment of Chinese AI models, for example prohibiting US companies from using the models both in the US and abroad and prohibiting US hyperscalers from making Chinese AI models available in the US or globally. This could either be an outright prohibition, or a restriction, e.g., Chinese models could only be used subject to certain conditions, such as security protocols. (There is some conceptual parallel to how the Department of Justice's Data Security Program works). (There would, however, still be the legal question about whether IEEPA could in fact prevent a US company from simply downloading and using a free Chinese open source model). 7. Congressional legislation: Congress could of course legislate new restrictions on the US use of Chinese AI models. This would avoid the IEEPA limitations discussed above related to “information,” though would still be subject to the First Amendment. I could see the courts upholding a congressional ban on the use of even free open-source AI models despite the first Amendment by finding that such a ban passes “intermediate scrutiny.” (This was part of the basis on which SCOTUS upheld *Congress’s* 2024 legislation requiring a divestment of TikTok after lower courts enjoined Trump’s 2020 IEEPA-based ban). Note: this post is intended solely as a rundown of what the legal options for restrictions are, not a normative argument on what the US government should do. 🇺🇦🇨🇦 We held a substantive discussion with Canada’s Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Tim Hodgson @timhodgsonmt. The key topics were cooperation in the gas sector and nuclear energy. We aim to further diversify gas supply routes. Ukraine has proposed creating a strategic energy security bridge with Canada focused on the supply of Canadian LNG to Ukraine. Following the agreements reached by President of Ukraine @ZelenskyyUa and Prime Minister of Canada @MarkJCarney, we discussed with the Minister the preparation and benefits of concluding a long-term 30-year strategic energy agreement. We discussed Ukraine’s preparations for the upcoming winter, including the possibility of direct grant support from Canada for gas purchases for Ukraine in the amount of CAD 650 million, as part of the overall support package for Ukraine this year. Ukraine also invited Canadian suppliers to use Ukrainian underground gas storage facilities. Another important topic was the supply of energy equipment from Canadian manufacturers to Ukraine. We also touched upon nuclear energy cooperation. Ukraine is interested in Canada’s experience and opportunities in the development of SMRs — small modular reactors. We agreed that this area will become part of our strategic energy agreement. I thanked my colleague for Canada’s unwavering support for Ukraine and for Minister Hodgson’s personal role in advancing our energy partnership at various levels. We highly value the assistance provided through the Ukraine Energy Support Fund. Canada’s total contributions to the Fund have already reached CAD 90 million. _______ 🇺🇦🇨🇦 Провели предметну розмову з Міністром енергетики та природних ресурсів Канади Тімом Ходжсоном. Ключові теми – співпраця у газовій сфері та атомній енергетиці. Ми прагнемо максимально диверсифікувати маршрути постачання газу. Україна пропонує створити стратегічний міст енергетичної безпеки з Канадою, зосереджений на постачанні канадського LNG в Україну. За результатами домовленостей Президента України Володимира Зеленського та Прем'єр-міністра Канади Марка Карні обговорили з міністром енергетики підготовку та переваги укладення довгострокової стратегічної угоди в енергетиці на 30 років. Торкнулися теми атомної енергетики. Нам цікавий досвід і можливості Канади у розвитку SMR, малих атомних реакторів, домовилися, що це буде частиною нашої стратегічної енергетичної угоди. Подякував колезі за незмінну підтримку України й особисту роль міністра Ходжсона у розвитку нашого енергетичного партнерства на різних рівнях. Hold on: The Time for Policy Patience Is Not Over PIDE's latest Monetary Policy Assessment recommends that the State Bank of Pakistan (@StateBank_Pak) maintain the policy rate at 11.5 percent at its upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting. Although headline inflation has eased to 11.1 percent, underlying price pressures remain persistent, with elevated core inflation, volatile weekly prices, and higher petroleum costs continuing to pose upside risks. At the same time, economic recovery is gaining traction but remains uneven, with weak large-scale manufacturing suggesting limited demand-side inflationary pressures. Market signals also support a cautious approach. Treasury-bill yields remain closely aligned with the current policy rate, while improved reserves and strong remittance inflows provide policy space despite continuing external vulnerabilities. PIDE's policy recommendation is clear: maintain the policy rate at 11.5 percent. A gradual easing cycle should begin only when disinflation is firmly established, inflation expectations are well anchored, and external sector stability is sustained. The DNA’s ‘double helix’ structure was discovered thanks in part to Rosalind Franklin. Today is her birthday! In 1962, James Watson, Francis Crick, and Maurice Wilkins confirmed the molecular structure of DNA by relying heavily on Franklin’s hypotheses and photographs of DNA strands created with X-ray diffraction. The three men won the @NobelPrize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the double helix structure of DNA. While Franklin did not win a share of the Nobel Prize despite her essential contributions, her work has not been forgotten.

Frank and informal exchanges with fellow Foreign Ministers of China, Uzbekistan, Iran, and Tajikistan after the session of the SCO Council of Foreign Ministers in the beautiful Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan.

🔈 PR No. 1️⃣8️⃣8️⃣/2️⃣0️⃣2️⃣6️⃣ Visit of the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister of Pakistan Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Council of Foreign Ministers’ meeting in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyz Republic from 23-24 July 2026 🔗⬇️

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met with the Foreign Minister of Uzbekistan, Bakhtiyor Saidov @FM_Saidov, on the sidelines of the SCO CFM Meeting in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan. The two Ministers reaffirmed the strength of the Pakistan-Uzbekistan strategic partnership and reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation across trade, investment, connectivity, energy, culture, and people-to-people exchanges. They emphasized the importance of sustained high-level exchanges and closer engagement between the business communities of both countries to further expand economic ties. They also discussed cooperation at regional and multilateral forums. Both Ministers recalled the successful visit of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Pakistan earlier this year and underscored the importance of translating the understandings reached during the visit into tangible outcomes through timely implementation. The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments. Foreign Minister Saidov appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote regional peace and stability, including its role in facilitating the Islamabad MoU. Both sides expressed hope that dialogue and diplomacy would continue to pave the way for lasting peace and regional stability. The two Ministers agreed to remain in close contact.

Shri K. S. Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met with the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister of Kazakhstan, Yermek Kosherbayev, on the sidelines of the SCO CFM Meeting in Kyrgyzstan. The two leaders reviewed the positive momentum in Pakistan-Kazakhstan relations following the visit of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to Pakistan earlier this year and reaffirmed their commitment to implementing the understandings reached, including the 37 MoUs signed during the visit. They agreed to intensify cooperation in trade, investment, transport and regional connectivity, energy, people-to-people exchanges, and at multilateral forums. Foreign Minister Kosherbayev appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to advance regional peace and diplomacy. They also exchanged views on regional and global developments and reiterated their shared commitment to peace, stability, and prosperity. Foreign Minister Kosherbayev invited the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister to visit Kazakhstan, which he graciously accepted at a mutually convenient time.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus, Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov, on the sidelines of the SCO Council of Foreign Ministers (CFM) Meeting in Cholpon-Ata. The two sides reviewed Pakistan-Belarus bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation across diverse sectors. They also looked forward to the 9th Session of the Pakistan-Belarus Joint Ministerial Commission, to be hosted by Pakistan in Islamabad on 11–12 August 2026, as well as to continued high-level exchanges. The two leaders discussed ways to expand economic and trade cooperation, deepen collaboration in defence, agriculture, technology, and workforce exchange, and reaffirmed their commitment to the Roadmap for Comprehensive Cooperation (2025–2027). The two Ministers also exchanged views on regional developments and issues of mutual interest. Foreign Minister Ryzhenkov appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in facilitating dialogue during the U.S.-Iran situation and commended Pakistan’s continued efforts to promote regional peace and security.

Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL), DRDO has transferred three advanced materials technologies to SAIL. Manufacturing technology for DMR-249A and DMR-249BK grade steel billets were transferred to SAIL's Alloy Steel Plant, Durgapur. These billets are used in the construction of Naval Ships and Submarines. The manufacturing technology for DMR-249B steel plates (8-30mm thickness) was transferred to SAIL's Alloy Steel Plant, Durgapur and Rourkela Steel Plant. These steel plates are used in specialised naval construction. Dr R V Hara Prasad, DG(N&SM) handed over the Licensing Agreement for Transfer of Technology (LAToT) to SAIL in the presence of Dr R Balamuralikrishnan, Director DMRL. The transfer of technology to industry marks a significant milestone in strengthening indigenous materials capabilities for strategic defence applications

Man muss das gedanklich erst einmal hinbekommen: Da wird im Kanzleramt ein schon existierender Posten umetikettiert, um angeblich die „Kommunikation zwischen Bund und Ländern“ zu verbessern. Als ob ausgerechnet Philipp Amthor als Staatsminister das bürokratische Dickicht des Föderalismus entwirren würde. Es geht doch überhaupt nicht um Sachpolitik. Das Kind bekommt nur einen schicken Namen. In Wahrheit scharrt Friedrich Merz schlicht seine treuesten Gefolgsleute um sich. Wer auf Parteitagen brav klatscht und bedingungslos strammsteht, wird eben mit einem Büro im Machtzentrum belohnt. Doch die Aktion hat einen noch übleren Beigeschmack: Merz scheint im Inneren des Apparats eine Verschwörung gegen sich zu wittern. Amthor zieht da nicht als Brückenbauer ein, sondern als horchender Aufpasser. Ein persönlicher Spion des Kanzlers, der die eigenen Flurgespräche filtert und dem Chef steckt, wer intern den Aufstand probt. Dass die Länderkommunikation dadurch um keinen Deut besser wird, dürfte allen Beteiligten völlig egal sein. Hauptsache, der Kanzler hat seinen Hofberichterstatter direkt im Haus.

The Cuiyun Corridor Ancient Shu Road (the ancient road system to today's Sichuan province) stretches across Jiange county in Guangyuan and Zitong county in Mianyang, Sichuan province, with the Jiange section forming its principal route. Extending for 151 kilometers, the road is lined with thousands of ancient cypress trees, some dating back to the Qin (221-206 BC) and Han (206 BC-AD 220) dynasties. After more than two millennia, many still stand tall with dense, evergreen foliage. Paved with stone slabs and shaded by towering cypresses, the road winds through tranquil forests. It is home to the world's oldest, largest, and best-preserved avenue of planted roadside trees, with more than 7,000 ancient cypresses over 1,000 years old. The oldest is more than 2,300 years old, nicknamed "a wonder of the Ancient Shu Roads" and "a living fossil forest". chinabound.cn Travel with ease in China, and with meaning. #China #Sichuan #CuiyunCorridor #ChinaBound #ASnapshotOfChina

EL BANCO CENTRAL REALIZÓ UNA FUERTE COMPRA DE DÓLARES Y SUPERA LOS USD 13.000 MILLONES EN 2026 El Banco Central de la República Argentina (BCRA) hilvanó 134 jornadas consecutivas con saldo comprador de divisas tras adquirir USD 345 millones este viernes. De esta manera, la autoridad monetaria superó los USD 13.000 millones comprados en lo que va de 2026. Desde el comienzo de la cuarta etapa del programa monetario y cambiario en enero, el BCRA realizó adquisiciones por 13.101 millones de dólares. El equipo económico había fijado como objetivo anual un rango de entre USD 10.000 y USD 17.000 millones para 2026. Entre enero y julio de 2026, la oferta de dólares aumentó gracias a las liquidaciones del sector agropecuario, energético y minero, junto con la colocación de deuda en mercados internacionales por parte de empresas y gobiernos provinciales. Estos flujos permitieron al Banco Central captar una parte considerable de los dólares disponibles. Infobae 📎 bit.ly/4wl2nAh

महाराष्ट्रावर विठूमाऊलीची कृपादृष्टी सदैव राहो, राज्यात सुख-समृद्धी नांदो, शेतकरी सुखी-समृद्ध होवोत आणि जनतेच्या जीवनात आनंद व समाधान लाभो, अशी प्रार्थना त्यांनी विठूमाऊलीच्या चरणी केली. त्याचबरोबर पंतप्रधाान नरेंद्र मोदी यांनी देशाच्या तरुणाईसाठी सुरू केलेल्या विकास आणि नव्या संधींच्या प्रवासाला अधिक बळ मिळावे, प्रत्येक युवक-युवतीच्या आशा-आकांक्षा पूर्ण व्हाव्यात आणि विकसित भारताच्या निर्मितीचा संकल्प अधिक वेगाने साकार व्हावा, यासाठीही मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी भगवान श्री विठ्ठल आणि रुक्मिणी मातेच्या चरणी प्रार्थना केली. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या हस्ते आज पंढरपूर येथे मानाचे वारकरी दाम्पत्य श्री. बाळासाहेब माने व श्रीमती प्रभावती माने यांचा सत्कार करण्यात आला. यावेळी मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांच्या हस्ते 'श्री विठ्ठल निर्मल दिंडी पुरस्कार 2026' प्रदान करण्यात आले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, यंदा वारीने नवा उच्चांक गाठला असून 25 किलोमीटरपेक्षा अधिक अंतरापर्यंत भाविकांची रांग लागली आहे. मात्र, या सर्व भाविकांची अत्यंत चांगल्या प्रकारे व्यवस्था करण्यात आली आहे. श्री विठ्ठल नामाचा गजर करत भाविक दर्शन घेत आहेत. जगाच्या पाठीवर असा आनंदाचा सोहळा दुसरा नाही, जिथे कोणत्याही निमंत्रणाशिवाय लाखो वारकरी आपल्या विठुरायाच्या दर्शनासाठी पायी निघतात. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, पंढरपूर येथे भगवान श्री पांडुरंगाच्या दर्शनासाठी दरवर्षी लाखो भाविक येतात. भाविकांची सातत्याने वाढणारी संख्या लक्षात घेता अधिक प्रशस्त परिसर आणि आवश्यक पायाभूत सुविधा निर्माण करणे काळाची गरज आहे. त्यादृष्टीने यावर्षीच पंढरपूर मंदिर कॉरिडॉरच्या कामाला सुरुवात करण्यात येणार असून, ते पूर्ण झाल्यानंतर दर्शन व्यवस्था अधिक सुलभ, सुव्यवस्थित आणि सुरळीत होईल. वारकऱ्यांची सेवा हीच विठ्ठलसेवा मानत राज्य शासनाने यंदा शेतकऱ्यांसाठी कर्जमाफी आणि मोफत वीज देण्याचा ऐतिहासिक निर्णय घेतला, असेही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले. यावेळी मंत्री गिरीष महाजन, मंत्री जयकुमार गोरे, मंत्री आकाश फुंडकर, आमदार The New York Times, citing multiple people briefed on the matter, reports that President Donald J. Trump switched from the Qatari donated Boeing 747-8 to the legacy Air Force One during the NATO summit after the Secret Service received what officials deemed a credible threat that Iranian proxy forces were targeting the president and whatever aircraft he was traveling aboard. The Qatari donated 747-8 is currently serving as the VC-25B "Bridge" aircraft, a temporary presidential transport intended to fill the gap until Boeing delivers the long delayed next generation VC-25B fleet. According to the report, the threat was not specific to the aircraft itself, but the incident has renewed scrutiny over its defensive capabilities, as it lacks some of the advanced defensive systems carried by the current VC-25A and future VC-25B fleets. President Trump appeared to acknowledge those limitations earlier this week when, after being asked about the aircraft's lack of antimissile defenses, he told reporters the jet would soon be taken out of service to be "maxed out" with additional upgrades, a process that White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed would take approximately one month. Basically, we have the old system, led more or less by Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi, which is centered on infantry and artillery, and the new system, led by Fedorov, which is centered on drones, fiber-optic cables, and computer chips. Each requires a massive pipeline of resources, whether that's personnel, funding, or manufacturing capacity. The two systems don't overlap very much. So when Fedorov became defense minister a few months ago, he began shifting resources toward his preferred method of warfare. Syrskyi, understandably, had a bit of a coronary because there was no way he could defend a 1,000-mile-long front without continued investment in artillery and artillery shells. Both of them are right. Both of them are wrong. And now, both of them have been fired. So what's happening now is that President Zelensky is trying to balance these two factions so they can both function because both are essential. The reason the protests in Ukraine in support of Fedorov are continuing is that protesters have looked at the personnel Zelensky has appointed to replace Syrskyi and Fedorov and concluded that, so far, nothing has changed. And that's true.

The route would let the 1 GW facility avoid open-access charges and source power far more cheaply, but the Electricity Act, 2003, makes no provision for a deemed distribution licensee that isn't a government company, which Google is not. Drawing a parallel with the railways case, where the Supreme Court ruled in May that railways is a consumer and not a deemed distribution licensee, Dasgupta warns the Google move risks the same legal fate. 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump remains trapped because he still refuses to accept how much leverage Iran possesses. He still thinks overwhelming American power will eventually force Tehran to give in, and political scientist Ian Bremmer says that's the mistake keeping this war alive. Instead, Iran has shown it can keep raising the economic cost of the war without crossing Trump's red lines. Ian doesn't think Iran believes it can defeat the U.S militarily; it believes it can make continuing the war more painful than ending it. And so far, it's working. Trump keeps threatening to destroy Iran's infrastructure, eliminate its leadership and dramatically escalate the conflict. But Ian points to something more revealing than Trump's rhetoric: His actions. Despite months of fighting, Trump has avoided the biggest escalations. No ground invasion, no sustained campaign against Iran's energy sector, and no full-scale assault on the country's leadership. Even after American casualties, his instinct has repeatedly been to play them down rather than use them to justify a much wider war. And Tehran has noticed. It increasingly sees a president who talks like he's preparing for total war but behaves like someone searching for an exit. The bigger problem, Ian says, is inside the White House itself. Trump's advisers know the military and economic costs are mounting, and many want the war to end, but very few are willing to tell Trump the uncomfortable truth: Iran has far more leverage over how this ends than Washington expected. Until Trump accepts that reality, Ian believes a genuine compromise remains unlikely. @ianbremmer Video

On the Dangers of U.S Unilateralism Abroad The new era of great power competition between autocrats and democrats will be fierce, challenging, and enduring. I believe the free world has more resources, superior institutions, and better ideas than the autocratic world. At the same time, many of the challenges we face today, especially from China, are different and more complex than they were during the Cold War. China’s highly sophisticated strategy of multilateralism is far more successful than anything the Soviets tried or achieved. Beijing does not want to destroy the old international economic and political architecture, as the Soviets did. Instead, it has worked within existing institutions—the UN, the World Bank, the WTO—while simultaneously creating new ones, including BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), and the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Starting new international clubs, as well as fostering win-win outcomes for countries that join, is a conscious, deliberate strategy for advancing Chinese interests and influence globally. Last week, Xi launched one more international club: the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO). Through WAICO, Beijing hopes to shape the international rules governing artificial intelligence independently of the United States. At its founding meeting last week, 29 countries signed the founding agreement, with more expected to follow. Tragically, Trump has pursued the exact opposite strategy to Xi—exiting old international organizations and agreements and failing to create much new. If you weren't aware, I had a small part in helping design TLS 1.3 back in the day. Today, I presented some new work at the TLS working group meeting in Vienna to upgrade its the key schedule from SHA-2 (the workhorse) to Keccak, the algorithm behind SHA-3. This isn't because SHA-2 is broken. It's old, yes (happy 25th SHA-2), but it's still considered secure. The reason for the proposal is that Keccak has some nice properties that allow for neat optimizations and is just now being widely rolled out in software packages because it's a part of ML-KEM, the post-quantum algorithm being deployed across the Internet. With Keccak appearing in more and more software stacks, protocols are exploring taking advantage of its properties as a "sponge" construction. With this new Keccak key schedule, embedded devices and other implementations using pure post-quantum algorithms can do TLS without needing to keep SHA-2 around at all. It was a fun exercise in protocol design. The draft got a lot of support, including from the Keccak team themselves, which was a lovely endorsement. This new extension is not part of TLS yet, but if it gets adopted, you may start seeing sponges around more and more, protecting your data. ietf.org/archive/id/draft-su…

NITI Aayog, in partnership with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), convened the Japan–India Forum on Adopting Japanese Best Practices for India's Aspirational Districts and Blocks, bringing together policymakers, development practitioners, academia, and experts from both countries to strengthen bilateral cooperation and exchange knowledge for improving development outcomes. Ms. Nidhi Chhibber, CEO, NITI Aayog, highlighted the importance of taking the India–Japan partnership beyond the achievement of saturation and leveraging global expertise through the collaboration between NITI Aayog and JICA. Shri K. S. Rejimon, Mission Director, Aspirational Districts and Blocks Programme, emphasised that the objective is not to replicate Japanese models, but to adapt the principles underlying their success to India's diverse local contexts. Mr. Takuro Takeuchi, Chief Representative, JICA India, shared Japan's experience in achieving balanced regional development and reaffirmed the shared commitment to advancing inclusive and sustainable growth. The forum underscored the importance of institutional collaboration, knowledge exchange, and locally relevant, evidence-based solutions in accelerating progress across Aspirational Districts and Blocks while further strengthening the India–Japan partnership. #PMOIndia #JapanIndia #AspirationalDistricts #KnowledgeExchange @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

Prof. K.V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, along with officials from NITI Aayog, visited Karnataka on 23–24 July to engage with the State Government on key development priorities. During the visit, Prof. Raju met the Chief Minister, the Chief Secretary, and senior officials of the State Government. Discussions focused on the methodology for estimating District Domestic Product and Primary Sector GDP, as well as NITI Aayog's collaboration with the State in preparing the Viksit Rajya @2047 Vision Document for Karnataka. In the first episode of @WHO_Europe's new podcast series, “I Believe You,” I speak with colleagues Melanie and Greg about the health sector’s role in responding to violence against women and girls. For many survivors, a health worker may be the first, and sometimes the only, person they turn to. Yet not all health workers are equipped to recognise the signs or provide the necessary support. When almost 1 in 3 women and girls aged 15 and older in our Region experience physical or sexual violence in their lifetime, the health sector cannot afford to be unprepared. This is why I launched a special initiative to strengthen the health sector’s response to violence against women and girls. Training health workers is an essential part of this effort, but it must go hand in hand with the right policies and clear clinical guidance. I am encouraged by the willingness of government leaders to support this work. It is time to turn that commitment into practical change. Strong partnerships are the foundation of everything @IFAD achieves, and they are central to IFAD’s work in Africa – a continent central to our mission of investing in rural people. As a net food-importing country, Djibouti is particularly exposed to disruptions in maritime transport and rising costs for food, agricultural inputs and machinery. We discussed the need to strengthen domestic productive capacity and food sovereignty through climate-smart agriculture, sustainable water infrastructure, modernized livestock and horticulture value chains, and greater private-sector participation. Agriculture is a cornerstone of Cameroon's economy, contributing around 20–22% of GDP and supporting livelihoods for over 60% of the population. Given that weight, Minister Mbairobe and I discussed the importance of keeping momentum across the portfolio by accelerating the effectiveness of approved investments and strengthening the delivery of cofinanced programmes. We also discussed the next Country Strategic Opportunities Programme and the value of a strong evidence base to guide our future cooperation. Senegal hosts one of IFAD's largest programmes in West and Central Africa, reflecting a shared commitment to agricultural transformation, youth employment and food sovereignty. In reaffirming that longstanding partnership, with Minister Ba, we welcomed our expanding cooperation, including through additional financing for two ongoing investments programmes: AGRIJEUNES and the Support to Food Sovereignty Programme. We exchanged views on how the strategic directions of #IFAD14 align with Senegal's own vision for agricultural transformation and our joint investments with #Italy under the #MatteiPlan. These discussions underscored the value of country ownership, coordinated investment and partnerships with governments, producers, development institutions and the private sector to accelerate rural transformation and strengthen foodsecurity. #FinancingTheFirstMile

#Bilawal Bhutto Zardari VS #Maryam Nawaz Sharif Political #Connection and the Kashmir #Constituency The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) has long enjoyed a reliable and deeply rooted political constituency in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. It is, therefore, difficult to avoid the impression that Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has not given this important political and historical asset the attention it deserves. What was inherited as a political advantage appears, at times, to have been treated as something that would remain available without requiring the same degree of political investment, emotional connection, or sustained direct engagement with the people. Bilawal Bhutto's political addresses in Azad Kashmir have, in my view, #lacked the distinctive sense of empathy and moral urgency once demonstrated by his #mother, Benazir Bhutto, who, while addressing the UN Human Rights Commission, appealed to the world to "open your hearts to the tragedy of Kashmir." That profound humanitarian appeal reflected a deeper understanding of the pain and aspirations of the Kashmiri people. #By comparison, #Bilawal's public addresses in Azad Kashmir have often sounded more like conventional electoral rhetoric, without that special emotional and human touch that could have strengthened his connection with the people. The #contrast was particularly noticeable during the visits of #Nawaz Sharif and #Maryam Nawaz Sharif to Muzaffarabad and Mirpur. Their engagement appeared to reach beyond routine politics and touch a deeper sense of identity and belonging. Nawaz Sharif made a particularly memorable point when he said, in effect, "It is not Kashmore; it is Kashmir. It is not Mirpur Khas; it is Mirpur."His words conveyed an understanding that Kashmir is not merely another electoral constituency but a place with its own history, identity, and emotional significance. He also embraced the legendary description of the people of Kashmir as "People of Legend"—a phrase that resonated with the dignity and historical consciousness of the Kashmiri people. Maryam Nawaz Sharif took this sense of personal connection even further. She spoke of her family's Kashmiri roots, referring to her father, mother, paternal grandparents, and maternal grandparents, and declared that she was a Kashmiri by heart, by mind, by intellect, and by spirit. Whatever one's political assessment may be, this was a powerful way of presenting herself not simply as a visiting politician but as someone claiming a place within the emotional and cultural identity of the people. Her visit was also accompanied by a tangible #gesture of public service—the provision of two fleets of air-conditioned electric buses for Muzaffarabad and Mirpur. Such initiatives may be viewed as political gestures, but they also #demonstrated preparation, attentiveness, and an understanding that political goodwill is strengthened when words are accompanied by something concrete for the people. By contrast, #Bilawal Bhutto's visit appeared to rely largely on the familiar language of #electoral politics, without a comparable initiative or a distinctive gesture that could have created a lasting impression. The Government of #Sindh, with its considerable resources, could perhaps also have considered a #meaningful contribution to the #people and institutions of Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The broader lesson is that political loyalty cannot be sustained by inheritance alone. A constituency may be historically reliable, but it must still be respected, understood, and continually earned. Nawaz Sharif and Maryam Nawaz Sharif appeared to recognise this during their #engagement with #Muzaffarabad and #Mirpur. Their #language, personal #identification with Kashmir, and tangible #gestures created a sense of emotional #connection that went beyond the conventional politics of an election campaign. For #Bilawal Bhutto and the PPP, the #challenge is not merely to retain a traditional vote bank in Azad Kashmir, but to rediscover the human, historical, and moral connection that once gave the party a special place in the hearts of many Kashmiris. ठीक 15 साल पहले… सुबह का सूरज भी नहीं निकला था, लेकिन कानपुर और लखनऊ में एक इंजीनियरिंग परीक्षा का प्रश्नपत्र खुलेआम बिक रहा था — कीमत थी ₹6 लाख। उस समय देश के शिक्षा मंत्री कपिल सिब्बल थे और सीबीएसई के चेयरमैन विनीत जोशी। AIEEE परीक्षा सीबीएसई ही कराती थी। उधर देशभर में लाखों छात्र परीक्षा केंद्रों पर बैठ चुके थे। इधर उत्तर प्रदेश पुलिस ने पेपर लीक का खुलासा किया और इसकी जानकारी दिल्ली तक पहुंची। सवाल उठे, लेकिन किसी बड़े स्तर पर जवाबदेही तय नहीं हुई। नया प्रश्नपत्र भेजकर दोबारा परीक्षा करा दी गई और मामला ठंडा पड़ गया, जैसे कभी कुछ हुआ ही नहीं। ऐसी घटनाओं ने समय के साथ पेपर लीक की समस्या को और गंभीर बना दिया। आज तस्वीर अलग है। पेपर लीक के मामलों में गिरफ्तारियां होती हैं, सख्त कानूनों के तहत कार्रवाई होती है, जांच तेज होती है, अधिकारियों पर जवाबदेही तय होती है और सरकार पर लगातार दबाव बना रहता है। सोशल मीडिया ने भी हर मामले को राष्ट्रीय बहस का विषय बना दिया है। बस यही सबसे बड़ा फर्क है। 2011 में बहुत कम लोगों ने पूछा था कि जिम्मेदारी कौन लेगा, जांच कहां तक पहुंची और किस पर कार्रवाई हुई। आज जनता सवाल भी पूछती है और जवाब भी मांगती है। लोकतंत्र में यही जागरूकता व्यवस्था को बेहतर बनाने की सबसे बड़ी ताकत है। प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी की सरकार लगातार इस व्यवस्था को और सुदृढ़ करने के लिए प्रयासरत है। Video

सहाय्यता कक्षाचा 'चरणसेवा' या उपक्रमांचा समारोप समारंभ पार पडला. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, वारीची परंपरा प्राचीन काळापासून शतकानुशतके अखंड सुरू आहे. महाराष्ट्रासह आसपासच्या राज्यांतून आषाढी आणि कार्तिकी वारीच्या निमित्ताने भागवत धर्माची पताका खांद्यावर घेऊन लाखो वारकरी पायी पंढरीकडे मार्गक्रमण करतात. मोगलांच्या आक्रमणाच्या काळात आणि इंग्रजांच्या राजवटीतही ही वारी कधीच थांबली नाही. सर्व संकटांवर मात करत ही परंपरा अखंड सुरू राहिली. महाराष्ट्रासारख्या पुरोगामी राज्यात आणि भक्तिमार्गाची राजधानी असलेल्या या भूमीत वारकऱ्यांसाठी सर्वोत्तम सेवा-सुविधा उपलब्ध करून देणे, हे आपले कर्तव्य आहे. पालखी मुक्कामाची गावे आणि पंढरपूरमधील रोगराई व दुर्गंधीची समस्या सोडविण्यासाठी 2016 मध्ये प्रथमच 'निर्मल वारी' उपक्रम सुरू करण्यात आला. त्यानंतर 2017 मध्ये राज्याच्या अर्थसंकल्पात त्यासाठी तरतूद करून हा उपक्रम अधिक व्यापक करण्यात आला असल्याचे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. वारीत चालून थकलेल्या वारकऱ्यांसाठी मुख्यमंत्री सहायता कक्षामार्फत 'चरणसेवा' हा विशेष उपक्रम राबविण्यात येत आहे. हा उपक्रम राबविताना युवा डॉक्टर आणि स्वयंसेवक अत्यंत भक्तिभावाने सेवा करताना दिसले. खऱ्या अर्थाने भारताच्या युवा शक्तीचे दर्शन यामधून घडते. त्यांची सेवा पाहिल्यानंतर भारताची संस्कृती काय आहे आणि महाराष्ट्र धर्माचे खरे स्वरूप काय आहे, हे स्पष्टपणे जाणवते, असे प्रतिपादन मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी केले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, यावर्षी 14 जिल्ह्यांमध्ये वारीचे अत्यंत सुयोग्य नियोजन करण्यात आले. या व्यवस्थेबाबत वारकऱ्यांनीही समाधान व्यक्त केले आहे. यामध्ये 5000 फिरती शौचालये, पिण्याच्या शुद्ध पाण्याची व्यवस्था तसेच स्वच्छतेसाठी आवश्यक सुविधा उपलब्ध करून देण्यात आल्या आहेत. तसेच पंढरपूरचे वाळवंट स्वच्छ करून चंद्रभागा नदी निर्मळ करण्यात आली आहे. पंढरपूरमध्ये 30 ते 35 लाख वारकरी येऊन गेल्यानंतरही पंढरपूर स्वच्छ राहील, अशी व्यवस्था करण्यात आली आहे. यावेळी मंत्री गिरीष महाजन, मंत्री I had the honor of welcoming @LauraLoomer —one of the most famous American political bloggers, whose views have a significant influence on the U.S. audience and who is well known for her close ties to President Donald Trump—to the Central Synagogue of Ukraine It is particularly valuable that Laura came to Ukraine in person. Previously, as she herself has publicly acknowledged, many of her perceptions of Ukraine were shaped by Russian propaganda. Like many people around the world, she was particularly troubled by Russia’s claims of alleged “Nazism” in Ukraine and the plight of the Jewish community here. That is precisely why she decided to come here to see everything with her own eyes. The conversation was candid. I told Lori the truth about this terrible war—about the daily Russian shelling, the children and civilians killed, the destroyed cities and villages, and the pain that Ukrainian families endure every day. I also shared my own personal tragedies—what I myself and our community have had to go through during these years of war. We also talked a lot about the lives of Jews in Ukraine. I explained that the Jewish community lives here openly, freely practices its faith, restores synagogues, builds Jewish schools, helps people, and is an integral part of Ukrainian society. Unfortunately, it is Russian propaganda that has, for many years, tried to impose a completely false image of the situation in Ukrainian society on the world. I’m glad that Laura came specifically to see everything with her own eyes and to understand what the heroic people of Ukraine are going through today. As a memento of our meeting, I gave Laura a copy of my book, *Between Miracle and Reality*. I hope it will help her gain an even deeper understanding of life in Ukraine, its people, and the true miracles we are now witnessing I sincerely thank Laura for her courage in coming here despite all the dangers, and for her desire to seek the truth! May the Almighty bless her, grant her wisdom, health, and protection, and help her always stand on the side of truth and justice!

Let's unpack the options for what the US government could do to potentially restrict Chinese AI models: 1. FUD: @deanwball noted the other day that the US government could take a "FUD" approach of just creating lots of doubt and uncertainty about use of Chinese AI, rather than strict legal requirements. (Dean made this point as an analytic matter, he was not advocating for it). The government could issue public security advisories, get sectoral regulators like energy and financial regulators to start raising risks, etc. This might not legally prohibit use, but would likely discourage it. 2. Procurement bans: The U.S. government could use procurement authorities to prohibit the use of Chinese AI models in government contracts, similar to what DoD did to Anthropic earlier this year. This would not prohibit private companies from using Chinese AI models unrelated to government contracts, but it would discourage use and reinforce a FUD approach. 3. Entity List: The Commerce Department could put specific Chinese AI companies (Moonshot, etc.) on the Entity List, which would prohibit exports of US technology to them. Setting aside evasion, this would cut off their access to any remaining US-origin chips not already covered by more general export controls and to US software. It would also potentially complicate U.S. companies’ use of closed or hosted models, as a US company could not send its own software or other "items" to the Chinese company for processing. It would not, however, strictly legally prohibit a U.S. company from downloading an open source model that a Chinese AI company posted online, as the download would not be an export *to* China, but rather an import from it. 4. "ICTS" rule: Commerce's existing "ICTS rule" allows Commerce to restrict the import or US use of a variety of software and other technology that poses a national security risk. Commerce has used the ICTS rule to, inter alia, prevent Americans from using Kaspersky Lab software (from Russia) and it is the basis for the recently-in-the-news restrictions on Polestar autos. Commerce could in theory deploy the rule to prohibit US firms from using Chinese AI models in the US. The one potential caveat to this is that the ICTS Rule exists pursuant to IEEPA, and IEEPA cannot regulate the import (or export) of "information" or "informational materials." I think courts would almost certainly uphold the ICTS rule as applied to the import or use of Chinese-hosted AI models as a prohibition on a “service,” and not on “information.” There would, however, be an interesting question about whether the courts would uphold a ban on a simple US download of an open-source Chinese model, where there was no payment. 5. Sanctions on Chinese AI labs: The President could use IEEPA to impose sanctions on Chinese AI labs, likely after declaring a new national emergency related to adversarial country AI risks. This would block their property in the US and prohibit all US commercial transactions with them. However, IEEPA sanctions would have the same carve out for "information" or "informational materials" as applies to the ICTS rule, and there is some chance the courts would find that IEEPA sanctions cannot prevent a US company from downloading, for free, an open source Chinese model. (Courts, for example, blocked Trump's 2020 use of IEEPA to try to restrict TikTok in the United States). 6. New IEEPA-derived restrictions on US companies using/deploying Chinese AI models: IEEPA is a flexible statute and the Trump Administration could use IEEPA to create new restrictions on the use or deployment of Chinese AI models, for example prohibiting US companies from using the models both in the US and abroad and prohibiting US hyperscalers from making Chinese AI models available in the US or globally. This could either be an outright prohibition, or a restriction, e.g., Chinese models could only be used subject to certain conditions, such as security protocols. (There is some conceptual parallel to how the Department of Justice's Data Security Program works). (There would, however, still be the legal question about whether IEEPA could in fact prevent a US company from simply downloading and using a free Chinese open source model). 7. Congressional legislation: Congress could of course legislate new restrictions on the US use of Chinese AI models. This would avoid the IEEPA limitations discussed above related to “information,” though would still be subject to the First Amendment. I could see the courts upholding a congressional ban on the use of even free open-source AI models despite the first Amendment by finding that such a ban passes “intermediate scrutiny.” (This was part of the basis on which SCOTUS upheld *Congress’s* 2024 legislation requiring a divestment of TikTok after lower courts enjoined Trump’s 2020 IEEPA-based ban). Note: this post is intended solely as a rundown of what the legal options for restrictions are, not a normative argument on what the US government should do. IFAD and the Government of South Sudan launched the Sustainable Agriculture Development Project (SADEP), a US$41.8 million investment to strengthen food security, build resilience and improve rural livelihoods for more than 110,000 people across the country. SADEP will also support the development of resilient fisheries value chains, contributing to the Government’s goal of positioning South Sudan as a fish-exporting country by 2027. “This project advances our national priorities to transition from humanitarian dependence to resilient and productive food systems. In partnership with IFAD, SADEP will empower farmers, fishers, women, and youth to strengthen livelihoods, with a clear commitment to scale results nationwide,” said Onyoti Adigo Nyikwec, Minister of Livestock and Fisheries of the Republic of South Sudan. شریف نے افتتاحی تقریب سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ متحرک، ترقی پسند اور شاندار مستقبل کے لیےسکائی 47 منصوبہ انتہائی اہم پیش رفت ہے،مشکلات اور چیلنجز کا امید اور حوصلے سے مقابلہ کریں تو معرکہ حق جیسے تاریخی کارنامے جنم لیتے ہیں،یہ منصوبہ پاکستان کے مستقبل کی ضمانت ہے اور ملک کو ناقابل تسخیر سکیورٹی فراہم کرے گا،متحد ہو کر کام کریں تو کوئی بھی ہدف ناقابل حصول نہیں۔ تقریب میں چیف آف آرمی سٹاف و چیف آف ڈیفنس فورسز فیلڈ مارشل سید عاصم منیر، وفاقی وزراء اور دیگر نے بھی شرکت کی۔وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ سکائی 47 ڈیٹا سینٹر قراقرم ون کی افتتاحی تقریب میں شرکت میرے لیے باعث اعزاز ہے،جدید ترین ڈیٹا سینٹر انتہائی متاثر کن اور قابل تحسین ہے،عظیم منصوبے کا مشاہدہ کر کے بے حد خوشی ہوئی ہے جو انتہائی مختصر مدت میں غیر معمولی عزم ،پختہ یقین اور اعلی مہارت کے ساتھ مکمل کیا گیا ہے. وزیراعظم نے مزید کہا کہ اگر ہم اس ماڈل پر عمل پیرا رہیں تو نہ صرف ہم ماضی کے نقصان کا ازالہ کرپائیں گے بلکہ مستقبل کے لئے انتہائی متحرک ترقی یافتہ پاکستان بنا سکیں گے جو وقت کی ضرورت ہے، یہ کام مشکل ہے لیکن ناممکن نہیں جس طرح کہ معرکہ حق میں ہم نے عظیم کامیابی حاصل کی جو پاکستان کی تاریخ کا عظیم ترین لمحہ تھا۔وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ جب انسان کا عزم پختہ ہو تو سب کچھ ممکن ہے،چیلنجز اور مشکلات آتی ہیں لیکن اگر مشکلات اور چیلنجز کے مقابلے کے لیے امید ،حوصلہ اور توانائی ہو تو معرکہ حق جیسے تاریخی کارنامے جنم لیتے ہیں۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ سکائی 47 جیسے عظیم منصوبے پاکستان کے مستقبل کی ضمانت ہیں ،فیلڈ مارشل سید عاصم منیر کی بصیرت افروز قیادت، شراکت دار زیڈ ٹی ای،وفاقی وزیر انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی اور سیکرٹری انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی کو بھرپور حمایت پر خراج تحسین پیش کرتا ہوں،قوم کو سکائی 47 جیسا تحفہ دینے پر تمام سٹیک ہولڈرز کا مشکور ہوں، مسلسل محنت ایسے عظیم منصوبوں کو حقیقت کا روپ دیتی ہے،اسی طرح کے منصوبے کراچی اور لاہور میں بھی مکمل کئے جائیں گے،تمام سرکاری اداروں کو اس سہولت سے منسلک کرنا چاہیئے۔ وزیراعظم نے اپنے خطاب میں مزید کہا کہ یہ منصوبہ پاکستان کے عوام کے لئے ایک بہترین تحفہ ہے جو ناقابل تسخیر سکیورٹی فراہم کرے گا اس منصوبے سے یہ امید اور حوصلہ ملتا ہے کہ اگر ہم متحد ہو کر کام کریں تو کوئی بھی ہدف ناقابل حصول نہیں۔قبل سینٹر کا افتتاح پاکستان میں مصنوعی ذہانت کے نئے دور کا آغاز ہے۔انہوں نے کہا کہ آج ایک نئے معاشی دور کے دروازے کھل رہے ہیں،ہم اپنے وسائل اور افرادی قوت سے بھرپور فائدہ اٹھا سکیں گے، ڈیٹا سے حاصل ہونے والی بصیرت مستقبل کی حقیقی معاشی طاقت ہے،مصنوعی ذہانت کی عالمی دوڑ محفوظ، کم لاگت اور مؤثر استعمال پر منحصر ہوگی۔انہوں نے کہا کہ مصنوعی ذہانت کے میدان میں آئندہ مسابقت ڈیٹا کے مؤثر استعمال پر اور ہماری ڈیجیٹل گنجائش بہت زیادہ ہے، ہمارا ای کامرس بزنس 25 سے 30 فیصد سالانہ کی شرح سے فروغ پا رہا ہے، اس ڈیٹا سینٹر کے ذریعے ملک میں ڈیجیٹل شعبے میں ایک مضبوط بنیاد رکھی جا رہی ہے۔ واضح رہے کہ سکائی 47 ڈیٹا سینٹر ٹیکنالوجی کے میدان میں خود انحصاری کی جانب اہم پیش رفت ہے،ڈیٹا سینٹر مصنوعی ذہانت ،مشین لرننگ اور ہائی پروفیشن کمپیوٹنگ کے تقاضے پورے کرنے کی صلاحیت رکھتا ہے،ڈیٹا سینٹر کلاؤڈ The Journal serves as a dedicated platform for diplomats, scientists, academics and policy practitioners to contribute to policy-relevant debate at the intersection of science, technology and international relations. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in collaboration with @OIC_COMSTECH, today launched the first issue of 2026 of the Journal of Science Communication and Diplomacy, celebrating two years of the Journal’s publication. In her keynote address, Foreign Secretary Ambassador Amna Baloch underscored that today’s global challenges require collective solutions, with science diplomacy playing an increasingly central role in bridging science and foreign policy. She emphasised the need for stronger scientific cooperation within the OIC and for developing countries to participate actively in shaping the governance of emerging technologies. Coordinator General COMSTECH Prof. Dr M. Iqbal Choudhary highlighted COMSTECH’s role as a platform for advancing scientific collaboration and harnessing the collective scientific potential of the Muslim world. 1/2

Dr. K.V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, along with officials from NITI Aayog, visited Karnataka on 23–24 July to engage with the State Government on key development priorities. During the visit, Dr. Raju met the Chief Minister, the Chief Secretary, and senior officials of the State Government. NITI Aayog convened a high-level consultation under the chairpersonship of Prof. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, with Shri Rajit Punhani, CEO, FSSAI, and Shri V. C. Sajjanar, IPS, Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad City, to deliberate on strengthening India's food safety architecture. The consultation brought together representatives from FSSAI, the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI), State Food Safety Departments, Hyderabad City Police, academic and research institutions, and technical experts to discuss strategies for enhancing food safety surveillance, strengthening enforcement mechanisms, and improving inter-agency coordination. I have stood firmly with the students and their movement from the very beginning. Their fight is not just for justice in the NEET scam- It is a fight to protect the future of every young Indian. The brutal crackdown by the Delhi Police on peaceful protesters is deeply disturbing and utterly unacceptable. Students were mercilessly beaten, lathi-charged, fired upon with pellet guns and subjected to tear gas simply for demanding accountability. So fearful is the Union Government of a peaceful democratic movement that it reportedly suspended internet services in and around Jantar Mantar and invoked the draconian National Security Act (NSA) to carry out preventive detentions of students- The very future of our nation. The Prime Minister speaks of zero tolerance towards corruption and promises strict accountability. Yet, only yesterday, the CBI stated that it found no evidence against the alleged kingpin in the 2024 NEET paper leak case. If those accused of destroying the future of lakhs of students continue to escape accountability, who is the government really protecting? Why is it so desperate to shield the Education Minister instead of answering the questions being raised by students across the country? The entire Opposition, along with the entire nation, stands firmly with our students and youth. I salute every young Indian for their indomitable spirit, unwavering courage, and refusal to bow before lathis, intimidation or the abuse of state power. India is proud of you all.

CM ने आगे कहा,' इस कठिन घड़ी में मेरी गहरी संवेदनाएं शोकाकुल परिवारों के साथ हैं. ईश्वर दिवंगत जनों की आत्मा को अपने चरणों में स्थान दें और शोक-संतप्त परिजन को इस असहनीय पीड़ा को सहने का संबल और शक्ति प्रदान करें. घटना की जानकारी मिलते ही उपायुक्त लाहौल-स्पीति से बात कर दोनों घायलों के बेहतर उपचार के निर्देश दिए हैं. उपायुक्त और घटनास्थल पर पहुंच रही हैं. ईश्वर से घायलों के शीघ्र और पूर्ण स्वास्थ्य लाभ की प्रार्थना करता हूं. ॐ शांति.' हदासे को लेकर पांगी के कार्यकारी आवासीय आयुक्त और SDM अमनदीप सिंह भी घटनास्थल के लिए रवाना हुए. वहीं, प्रशासन और बचाव दल मौके पर मलबा हटाकर गाड़ी तक पहुंचने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं. प्रशासन ने भी आम जनता से किसी भी तरह की अफवाहों को फैलाने और उन पर विश्वास न करने की अपील की है. #HimachalPradesh #RoadAccident #SpitiValley

President Droupadi Murmu met President of the Senate of Romania H.E. Mr Mircea Abrudean and President of the Chamber of Deputies of Romania H.E. Mr Sorin Grindeanu at the Parliament Palace in Bucharest. She also interacted with members of the India-Romania Parliamentary Friendship Group. Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Smt. Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, and Members of Parliament Dr. Dinesh Sharma and Shri Vijay Baghel were also present on the occasion. Such interactions would provide valuable opportunities to share experiences and best practices, and would contribute to further strengthening the India–Romania partnership.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 held a meeting with the Foreign Minister of Iran, Seyyed Abbas Araghchi @Araghchi, on the sidelines of the SCO CFM Meeting in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyz Republic. The two Ministers reaffirmed the close and longstanding ties between Pakistan and Iran and reviewed the evolving regional situation. DPM/FM expressed deep concern over recent regional tensions and underscored the importance of dialogue, restraint, de-escalation by all sides, and sustained diplomatic engagement to achieve lasting peace and stability. He emphasized the need to build on the understandings reached under the Islamabad MoU of June 2026. Foreign Minister Araghchi appreciated Pakistan’s continued diplomatic support and constructive efforts in promoting regional peace and security. He also thanked Pakistan for facilitating the safe return of Iranian fishermen and crew members, including those from vessels interdicted by the U.S.,and for its close coordination with the Iranian, U.S., and other relevant authorities to ensure their safe transit through Pakistan and return to Iran. The two sides agreed to maintain close coordination and regular consultations on issues of mutual interest and reaffirmed their commitment to working together for regional peace, stability, and shared prosperity.

Allow me to explain the core problem with the #EU #ageVerification concept. They're trying to solve an ontological problem with cryptography; something which is logically & demonstrably impossible. They're conflating a cryptographic, epistemic claim "this credential belongs to someone over 18" with the ontological "this person is over 18". Even perfect Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) do not bridge the gap between digital assertions and physical reality. There's not a cryptographic protocol on earth that does. The entire theatrical process establishes provenance. Provenance is not truth. I call it as escalation path precisely because this logical divide cannot be solved with code. It's not a technical problem. The developers have been tasked with solving the unsolvable. The question is simple: How old is ______________? How can you possibly answer that without vital context; the person's identity? So what's next in the global push for age verification? #ID checkpoints everywhere, real-time video/audio, geolocation, outlawed & undermined cryptography - traceability from end to end... to "protect the children" No #privacy, no rights... and no say in the matter. We're sleep walking into the abyss. Wake up.

Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, today participated in the High-Level Conference of High Contracting Parties to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC), in Manila, the Philippines, as part of the commemorative activities marking the Treaty’s 50th anniversary. Bringing together ASEAN Foreign Ministers and ministerial-level representatives of the High Contracting Parties to the TAC, the Conference underscored the Treaty's enduring relevance and growing global appeal over the past five decades. It reaffirmed the collective commitment of the High Contracting Parties to uphold the purposes and principles of the TAC and provided a platform to exchange views on strengthening cooperation in support of regional peace, stability, and prosperity.

Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, today held a bilateral meeting with the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment, and Tourism of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, Hon. Vijitha Herath, M.P., in Manila, Philippines, on the 50th anniversary of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC). Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening ASEAN-Sri Lanka relations and exchanged views on ways to enhance cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

The proposed center at Bicester Garrison in Oxfordshire could hold more than three times Piddington’s population and may begin operating by the end of 2026. Residents say they were informed only after the plan was already largely decided and fear the impact on local security, infrastructure, and public services. On July 4th, coinciding with the 250th anniversary of American independence, villagers held a preliminary vote on whether to organize an independence referendum. Of those who voted, 96% backed the proposal, with 175 votes in favor and seven against. Bicester is one of three military sites selected to accommodate around 3,750 asylum seekers. The others are RAF Linton-on-Ouse in North Yorkshire and RAF Barnham in Suffolk, where residents have also protested.
